## TL;DR

Added server-assisted tailnet discovery for the native Hub without giving the
phone a scanner or Tailscale/SSH access. `GET /api/servers/tailnet` reuses the
CLI's discovery code (moved to `src/core/tailnet-servers.ts`) and returns the
same rows plus a ready-to-open URL and an `https` flag; a per-host and
whole-request deadline turns a slow machine into an `unreachable` row instead of
hanging the request. Hub's picker now has **Find servers on my tailnet**, which
asks one saved server, shows a multi-select list that de-duplicates origins and
marks saved rows, and saves only explicitly picked HTTPS rows through the
existing `validateServer` reachability gate. Discovery can be turned off with
`tailnetDiscovery = false`, which has schema, Settings, supported-key and docs
entries.

## Work and rationale

**Shared discovery instead of a second implementation.** `parseTailnetPeers`,
`collectTailnetServers`, `serversSshArgs` and `ListedServer` moved from
`src/commands/servers.ts` to `src/core/tailnet-servers.ts`; the CLI re-exports
them so existing imports and tests keep working. The new
`src/server/routes/servers.ts` calls the same `collectTailnetServers`, so the
endpoint and `repoos servers --tailscale` cannot drift.

**URLs the phone can actually open.** A peer's registry port is not
necessarily its TLS port: `repoos serve` maps an HTTPS MagicDNS name (443, 8443
or 10000) to the server's loopback port through `tailscale serve`. Discovery now
reads `tailscale serve status --json` locally and on each peer and maps the
proxied loopback port to the resulting `https://<magicdns>[:port]` URL. When no
mapping exists it reports the honest `http://<magicdns>:<port>` with
`https: false` rather than inventing an HTTPS address. `tailscale serve status`
runs concurrently with `repoos servers --json` and is capped at 1.5 s, so a slow
serve-status call cannot hide otherwise good rows.

**Partial results and a deadline.** `collectTailnetServers` now takes
`deadlineMs`; every peer races against the remaining deadline and returns
`{ host, unreachable: true, reason: "timed out" }` on expiry. The endpoint uses
8 s overall, 4 s per SSH command. Local `tailscale status` is capped at 2 s.
Errors are preserved; a timeout is normalised to `timed out`.

**Auth and privacy.** The route is registered with the other authenticated
`/api/*` routes, so the existing middleware refuses anonymous requests; it is in
the UI-only allowlist in `src/cli/api-route-parity.ts` because the phone cannot
use the CLI and no CLI has to call its own HTTP endpoint. The phone makes
exactly one new outbound request, to a server the user already saved, and does
no scanning. Discovery can be disabled server-side; Hub then shows the server's
plain message and manual add is unchanged.

**Mobile merge logic is pure and tested.** `mobile/src/tailnet.ts` holds the
fetch result types, a timeout-aware `fetchTailnetServers`, and
`mergeTailnetResults`, which de-duplicates on host+port (so an HTTP and HTTPS
view of one server do not both appear), prefers the HTTPS row, marks saved
origins, keeps unreachable rows visible with their reason, and marks only
HTTPS, unsaved rows selectable. `app-state.ts` keeps discovery state and saves
picks sequentially through `addServer`; `TailnetDiscoveryView.vue` renders the
multi-select list with selection defaulting to none. A `fixture=discover`
scenario exercises the screen in browser dev.

**Config surface.** `tailnetDiscovery` defaults to `true`, is parsed in
`loadConfig`, has a live boolean entry in `getConfigSchema()` (rendered in the
General tab's Remote validation section), is in `SUPPORTED_TOML_KEYS`, and is
documented in `user-docs/configuration.md`. `docs/mobile-architecture.md` and
`mobile/README.md` now describe the server-assisted import, its privacy
properties and its limits.

## Approaches tried

I first considered having the phone call the existing tailnet logic through a
token or by reading the InAppBrowser's cookies, but the shell has no session for
the saved origin: server cookies live in the isolated InAppBrowser container,
and the server's JSON CORS reply is `*`, which browsers reject for credentialed
requests. I therefore send `credentials: "same-origin"` (so the web build served
by RepoOS carries its session, while the native cross-origin request stays
CORS-compatible) and surface a 401 as a plain message. Per-server shell
sessions are story task #0304; the docs state this caveat rather than claiming a
device flow works.

For URLs I rejected HTTPS-probing the registry port: `tailscale serve` may
terminate TLS on a different port, so only the serve config gives the real URL.
I also rejected duplicating discovery in the route; sharing the core function
was the smaller diff and keeps CLI output stable.

## Challenges and blockers

- The first scoped gate failed on `api-route-parity.test.ts` because the new
  endpoint had no CLI/allowlist entry. I added an exact UI-only matcher with the
  reason; the parity test now passes.
- The second gate's remote tests passed, but its follow-up local browser step
  failed `bun run smoke` once after a long remote run. `bun run smoke` and
  `bun scripts/ui-smoke.mjs` both pass locally on the same tree, twice, with no
  browser or mount error; this looks like the known headless-WebKit/managed-
  resource flake rather than a code failure. `repoos check --step ui-smoke`
  timed out waiting on remote validation, so I did not get a third full-gate
  result before handoff; RepoOS re-runs the gate server-side.
- Real-device verification on Nick's phone is still a human step. I did not run
  one, and the report makes no claim about device behaviour. Likewise, the
  authenticated path on an auth-enabled native install depends on #0304.

## Key learnings

- `tailscale serve` is the only reliable source of a phone-openable URL; a
  registry port and its TLS port are different things.
- A discovery endpoint must bound both the per-host work and the whole request;
  `Promise.all` alone still lets one peer hold the response open.
- The mobile shell and the isolated InAppBrowser deliberately do not share
  cookies, so "the phone already has a session" is false for the native shell
  until per-server sessions land. Documenting that is better than a hidden
  failure or an unauthenticated endpoint.
- De-duplicate on host+port, not full origin, or the HTTP and HTTPS views of the
  same server appear twice and only one is usable.
